title: The quasi-finite locus is open
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Using quasi-finiteness in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite], the set of points of $X$ at which $f$ is quasi-finite is an open subset $U\subseteq X$, and the induced morphism $U\to S$ is locally quasi-finite.

proof.text: Fix a point x of X at which f is quasi-finite. By [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1), choose affine opens U = Spec(B) containing x and V = Spec(A) containing f(U), such that the induced finite-type ring map A \to B is quasi-finite at the prime q of B corresponding to x.
Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-quasi-finite-locus-open] to A \to B and q. It gives an element g in B not contained in q such that A \to B_g is quasi-finite at every prime of B_g.

The basic open D(g) of Spec(B) is an affine open neighbourhood of x, with coordinate ring B_g; viewed as an open subscheme U_g of X, its canonical affine immersion is an open neighbourhood of x by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], and f(U_g) is contained in V. The induced map on this affine open and V is A \to B_g, which is of finite type since A \to B is and B_g = B[1/g]; so every point of U_g is quasi-finite for f by [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1) and step 2.

Every point of the quasi-finite locus has such an open neighbourhood U_g, while each U_g consists entirely of quasi-finite points. Therefore the locus is the union of these open subsets and is open in X.

Let U be the open locus of step 4 and x a point of U. The affine open U_g of step 3 around x lies in U, so U_g and V, with the finite-type ring map A \to B_g quasi-finite at the prime of x (step 2), witness [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1) for the induced morphism U \to S at x. Hence U \to S is quasi-finite at every point of U, i.e. locally quasi-finite by [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2).
